_readme: News archive for FootballSG. Append to items[]; never rewrite history. Every item needs a real source URL — an unsourced item must not ship. Dates must come from the article body, not a listing page: FAS listing pages mis-attribute dates. `time` is optional and Asia/Singapore — state it only when the source does; never invent one. Validated by checks/news-audit.mjs on every push.

items.title: Geylang top the SPL after Matchweek 3; Lion City Sailors rout Young Lions 6-1 in Mark Jackson's first league game
items.summary: Geylang International beat FC Jurong 3-1 at Our Tampines Hub to go top of the 2026/27 Singapore Premier League table on nine points after three matches. In the same round, Lion City Sailors thrashed Young Lions 6-1 at Jalan Besar Stadium on 11 October — new head coach Mark Jackson's first league match in charge — with Matthias Phaëton scoring twice.

items.title: Champions League matchday 2 sets all-time scoring record with 78 goals
items.summary: UEFA confirmed that Matchday 2 of the 2026/27 Champions League produced 78 goals across 18 matches on 13-14 October, the highest total for any matchday in the competition's history and seven more than the previous record of 71 set on Matchday 3 of 2025/26. Headline results included Liverpool 6-3 LASK, Aston Villa 6-0 Fenerbahce, Real Madrid's 4-3 comeback win at Roma and PSG's 4-2 win at Manchester City.

items.title: FAS confirms Singapore U-15 boys' squad and fixtures for inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival
items.summary: The Football Association of Singapore confirmed on 12 October that the national Under-15 boys' team will play five group matches in three days at the first-ever FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival, held 24-30 October in Baku, Azerbaijan. Singapore are drawn in Group P with Guatemala, Honduras, Canada, Guinea and American Samoa, with all matches at the Hovsan Competition Complex; players must be born in 2011 or 2012.

items.title: Gavin Lee names a 25-man Lions squad for the ASEAN Hyundai Cup 2026
items.summary: Head coach Gavin Lee confirmed the 25 players representing Singapore at the ASEAN Championship Hyundai Cup 2026, which runs from 24 July to 26 August. The Lions open their Group A campaign away to Cambodia in Phnom Penh on Friday 24 July, return home to face Timor-Leste on 27 July, then travel to defending champions Vietnam on 31 July.

items.title: Tickets released for Singapore's ASEAN Hyundai Cup home fixtures at Jalan Besar Stadium
items.summary: FAS put tickets for the Lions' home Group A fixture against Timor-Leste on sale at 11am, with tickets for the 7 August home fixture against Indonesia following on Wednesday 22 July, also at 11am. Both fixtures are at Jalan Besar Stadium.
